Is ArmA 3 worth $60? Mostly interested in the battle royal mode.

Arma is very much so a manual car, to Call of Duty being an automatic. The controls take some getting used to. It's not so much just like an FPS but a military simulator. Once you get used to all the inputs, it's not so bad.

That being said, Arma can be a lot of fun. All of the mods and custom games are what make the game fun in my opinion. If I play Arma, it's something like Altis Life, or Wasteland.

$60 is still kinda steep, but it get's put on steam sale a lot. I'd wait a bit honestly.

If you aren't sure you will like it, just wait for a sale and pick it up then. It usually goes down to half price during the big sales, and occasionally they have a weekend sale on Steam. It's definitely not a game for everyone, and you can get a lot of enjoyment out of that $60 in other ways.

That said, I thoroughly enjoy the game, though I play mil-sim stuff almost exclusively. It has a lot of potential, but you have to accept it with all its flaws as well. Things are wonky as hell sometimes, but you'll probably get used to writing things off as "Arma being Arma"

For me that "unpolished feeling" is still part of arma 3 (h1z1 is worse though). Its a simulation so some of the controls arent perfect but when youre used to it and playing with friends that game can be very intense and fun.

Yes. ARMA 3 by itself is so freakin' fun. From Battle Royale to King of the Hill to Wasteland. And that's without the mods. Once you start getting into Epoch, Breaking Point, etc, you'll understand why so many people own it. It's a versatile shooter platform that is home to a hell of a lot of fun. It may not be the best optimized but it's pretty good if you've got a decent machine. It's very pretty even on low settings. The combat feels a lot better compared to ARMA 2. It's slower than your CoD or your Battlefield, for sure, but it can still be hectic.

I agree with everyone else, the game is nothing like any other FPS game I can think of. The controls are a lot more complex and take a lot of getting used to. I've played the campaign for ARMA II and it was okay, never played it online. I only got the game for DayZ when it was still a mod.

The closest game I think I could compare it to is America's Army if that's even still around.

I'd highly suggest watching game-play of it, getting a pirated copy (if you're not opposed) to test it out or there is a free demo of ARMA II you can download.

It's a fantastic, massive game. I got over 700 hours in, and I'm not even remotely done with it yet. There are tons of actively developed mods for it. With mods and multiplayer particularly, you will need to make sure your CPU is up to the task.

There was a free weekend not that long ago, if you're still not sure, maybe wait for the next?
